items.subtitle: To Build a Republic of Spirit
items.title: A History of the Fulbright Program in Poland, 1945–2025
items.description:
Narrating the history of post-war intellectual encounters across the Iron Curtain, this book shows how the Fulbright Program quietly cultivated an Atlantic-minded elite in Poland from the late 1950s to today. It follows the programme through Cold War secrecy, surveillance and hard binational bargaining, revealing Washington’s blend of idealism and pragmatism and Warsaw’s calculated openness, as scholars, technocrats and future politicians built networks that outlasted communism.

The book reconstructs the ‘republic of the spirit’ they imagined – an ethical and intellectual fellowship beyond Party control – while tracing the circulation of ideas, expertise and cultural codes that shaped the 1989 transition and its aftermath. It examines how alumni legends were crafted and how daily compromises played out: democratic binationalism versus Party oversight, soft power versus security paranoia, mutual understanding versus image-management. In doing so, the book shows how international community-building actually worked, and why its foundations now feel precarious.

It also uncovers the Fulbright Program’s unintended consequences, from the rise of Poland’s pro-American ‘mandarins of the future’ to their constrained strategic autonomy in a world where US liberal internationalism is fading. As America pares back its post- 1945 role and loosens its own instruments of influence, the durability of this transatlantic community is uncertain. However, its legacy of shared mental maps, intellectual kinship and habits of cooperation still shapes Poland’s place in the world.

items.title: Jerzy Giedroyc – Zbigniew Brzezinski. Correspondence
items.description:
A documentary edition of the correspondence between Jerzy Giedroyc and Zbigniew Brzezinski, covering more than four decades of discussion about Poland, Ukraine, Russia, the Soviet Union, and American strategy toward Eastern Europe.

The project treats their correspondence not only as a record of two prominent intellectuals, but as an entry point into the networks connecting the Paris Kultura, American Sovietology, foundations, universities, and policy circles.
